Title: Monumenta fidei ecclesiae orientalis: primum in unum corpus collegit variantes lectiones ad fidem optimorum exemplorum adnotavit prolegomena addidit indice rerum praecipuarum instruxit Ernestus Julius Kimmel (Gennadii Confessiones I. II., Cyrilli Lucaris Confessionem, Confessionem Orthodoxam Ecclesiae Orientalis et Acta Synodi Hierosolymitanae complectens)
Creator: Compiled by Ernst Julius Kimmel (the title page calls him 'Ruthenus', licentiate in theology, formerly private lecturer at Jena; the catalogue gives 1812-1846); the 1850 printing carries a preface signed 'H. Weissenborn', Jena, October 1849. The confessions themselves are those of Gennadius (Confessions I and II), Cyril Lucaris, the Orthodox Confession (Mogila), and the Acts of the Synod of Jerusalem
Publisher: Jena: Frider. Mauke (Prostat apud Frider. Mauke), 1850 (title page MDCCCL)
Publication Date: 1850
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication); the item page carries possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
Language: grc (mixed: Greek confessions with facing Latin translations, and Kimmel's Latin prolegomena, notes and apparatus; the Greek is about one third of the text by letter count, so this is not a pure-Greek witness)
Source: Internet Archive item monumentafideie00kimmgoog, full-text OCR file monumentafideie00kimmgoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread, 2026-09-29. Item page marks possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Google scan of the New York Public Library copy.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged, apart from this header. Rights basis: 1850 publication date clears this registry's public-domain-by-date rule; the host's own NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT tag agrees. The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. OCR artifacts are left as found; nothing was corrected, re-spaced or retyped.
Content note: A 19th-century critical collection of the Eastern confessions, Greek with Latin; the Latin prolegomena, the variant readings and the indexes are the editors' scholarship, not the confessions' voice. The scan is a two-volumes-in-one binding. Order in the file: prolegomena; Gennadius's two Confessions; Cyril Lucaris's Confession (Greek and Latin); the Orthodox Confession (Confessio Orthodoxa), whose Pars prima, secunda and tertia are Faith, Hope and Charity, Greek and Latin in parallel; then the Synodus Hierosolymitana (the Synod of Jerusalem's acts). Greek OCR is partial and accented Greek has recognisable errors; treat the Greek as second witness for wording until checked against the page images, and the Latin translations as readable. Robertson's bibliography in the Acts and Decrees volume calls the 1850 printing a reprint of Kimmel's Libri Symbolici Ecclesiae Orientalis (Jena, 1843) with additional matter; the 1843 printing is not vendored.

Muham. Utrum loco capiatur Deus an non? 


Gennad. Animadverte et intelliges diligenter, quod

minatus est Jesus et appellatus Christus. Igitur Christus 
filius et verbum Dei est incarnatus, habens formam hominis.

Interrogatio tertia. 
Quosnam libros Scripturae 
nomine dignaris ? 


Responso. 

Sacram Scripturam Cano- 
nicos omnes libros sppella- 
mus, quos tanquam fidei ac 
salutis nostrae regulam acce- 
pimus atque adeo retinemus, 
eaque potissimum de causa, 
quod divinitus inspiratam no- 
bissuggerant doctrinam, quae 
tum ad institutionem tum ad 
illuminationem et perfectio- 
nem illius, qui ad fidem ac- 
cedit, sufficiat: hunc vero 
canonicorum librorum nume- 
rum esse credimus, quem La- 
odicensis Synodus pronun- 
tiavit, et quem Catholica et 
Orthodoxa Christi Ecclesia a 
Spiritu Sancto illuminata in 
hunc usque diem confitetur. 
Atii, quos Ápocryphos appel- 
lamus, hoc propterea nomine 
insigniuntur, quod eandem 
a Spiritu Sancto autoritatem 
et approbationem non acce- 
perint, quam qui proprie et 
citra controversiam pro Ca- 
nonicis habentur, quorum ex 
numero sunt, Pentateuchus, 
Hagiographa ac Prophetae, 
quos Laodicensis Synodus le- 
gendos esse statuit, veteris 
nempe testamenti libros vi- 

inti duos. Ex novo vero 
infer opes nostras recense- 
mus quatuer Evangelistas, 
Acta Apostolorum, Epistolus 
S. Pauli et Catholicas, qui- 
bus etiam addimus Apoca-

Quotuplex est peccatum? 


Resp. Ex sententia Scri- 
pturae aliud est peccatum 
ad mortem, aliud non ad mor- 
tem. Sunt igitur alia pec- 
cata mortalia alia non item. 


Quaestio XVIII 
Quid est peccatum mortale ? 


Resp. Mortale pecca- 
tum est, quando perversa ho- 
minis cupiditas facinus ali- 
quod divino praecepto pla- 
ne vetitum designat; aut 
rursus non sua sponte, ple- 
noque arbitrio suo, id prae- 
stat, quod a Deo jussum 
est; unde Dei proximique 
caritas refrigeratur. Hujus- 
modi cupiditas hominem a 
gratia Dei excludit, eum- 
que, qui illam opere ipso 
perpetrat, interimit. Qua 
etiam re ejusmodi pecca- 
tum mortale appellare didi- 
cimus; auctore Apostolo 


(Rom. VI, 23.): &Stipen- 
dium peccati mors est. Nu- 
da vero consensio, per 
quam peccatum se commis- 
surum quispiam destinat, 
grave ila quidem animae 
vulnus imponit, non tamen 
penitus enecat.

Quaestio XXIV. 
Quid est superbia? 


Resp. Superbia est ín- 
ordinata et injusta gloriae 
suae ambitio, ut super alios 
sibi aequales, qua jure qua 
injuria, emineat. Hoc pec- 
catum omnium primum erat, 
quod in Lucifero exorieba- 
tur; ex quo, velut ex suf- 
fusa veneno scaturigine, ce- 
tera omnia promanarunt. De 
eo sic ait Sapientia (Pro- 
verb. VIII, 13.): Timor Do- 
mini odit injustitiam et in- 
juriam et superbiam et vias 
improborum. Et alibi Scri- 
ptura (Sirach. X, 7.): Odi- 
osa coram Domino et ho- 
minibus est superbia. Huic 
vitio contraria humilitatis vir- 
tus est, quam Dominus no- 
ster lesus Christus com- 
mendans, nosque ad illam 
amplectendam adhortans, sic 
loquitur (Matth. XI, 29.): 
Discite a me, quod mitis 
sum, et humilis corde, et 
invenietis requiem animabus 
vestris.

textum graecum huic quoque Appendici inserere.

regione Ruthenica quae me tulit oriundum citius literis 
ereptum, defunctus — non solum reliquiis ejus litteraris 
editis, sed etiam indice alphabetico rerum memorabilium 
hac Appendice contentarum confecto et indice Eixrratorum 
et Addendorum ad priorem librorum symbolicorum partem 
adjecto — hoc unum in optatis habeo, ut ne illius me- 
moria intereat, sed in honore sit et colatur ab omnibut, 
qui ejus vel scripta perlegerunt vel scholas frequentaruat, 
vel consuetudine et familiaritate usi sunt. — ΜῈ d
